revenue: tens of millions USD cumulative; 27M players as of 2026 (per Wikipedia + poncle reports)
why_worked: Started as a weekend/nights side project on a full-time salary (near-zero financial risk), used a cheap web-friendly framework (Phaser) first, then ported to Unity once revenue proved the concept; a single addictive core loop (auto-attack, exponential power scaling) with near-zero content-authoring burden per session made it solo-scalable.
failure_modes: viral breakout is extremely rare and not repeatable by design
budget under $1,500 masks the years of prior game-dev skill-building that made rapid execution possible
team grew to 6+ after success, so the true solo-only revenue window was short

revenue: $1M in first 8 hours; 5M+ copies sold; mobile port $4.2M net revenue since Sept launch
why_worked: Recombined two universally-known mechanics (poker hands + roguelike deckbuilding) so the pitch was instantly legible; minimalist scope (single screen, no 3D art pipeline) fit a lightweight scripting engine (LÖVE/Lua) a solo dev could ship fast; publisher partnership (Playstack) handled marketing/porting after the core game proved itself.
failure_modes: extreme outlier — most deckbuilders do not recombine two mass-familiar mechanics this cleanly
solo dev still needed a publisher deal to scale beyond Steam
genre (roguelike deckbuilder) is now saturated post-Balatro, harder to repeat the surprise factor

revenue: 8M+ players within a year of launch (pre-console)
why_worked: Free-engine (Godot, zero licensing cost) kept a single dev's overhead near zero; simple real-world-object premise (a shotgun + Russian roulette) was instantly streamer/clip-friendly, which drove organic Twitch/YouTube discovery without a marketing budget.
failure_modes: streamer-driven virality is not a repeatable acquisition channel on demand
short, shock-value core loop has a content ceiling; needed a paid full sequel/expansion to sustain revenue

revenue: $151M gross on Steam in 2025; 414,000 concurrent players opening weekend
why_worked: Rode a taboo/high-novelty premise (drug empire sim) that no major studio would greenlight, into a starved niche of simulation/tycoon fans; Early Access let revenue and community feedback compound before full launch marketing spend.
failure_modes: single most extreme outlier found in this entire search pass — not representative of any base rate
taboo-premise strategy carries platform/policy risk (storefront delisting, payment-processor risk) that a risk-averse operator should weigh

why_worked: 4.5 years of solo full-time development (self-taught art+code+music+design in one person) produced unusually high content depth and polish per-dollar; nostalgia hook (Harvest Moon successor) gave an existing, underserved fan base built-in demand at launch.
failure_modes: 4.5-year unpaid solo runway is not financially available to most operators
success required becoming expert-level in art, music, AND code simultaneously — a rare skill combination
